subject: Anchored VPC segmentation - diagram clarity & egress separation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lia Robinson <lia.robinson@edgeworks.com>, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@paloaltopartner.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Anchored VPC segmentation - diagram clarity & egress separation

Hi Lia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for walking through the project constraints yesterday. I attached an updated "anchored-vpc-diagram-v3.pdf" (focused view: control plane vs data plane) and a draft tenant routing matrix. Before the architecture review call tomorrow I want to make sure we're aligned on three specific items where we've seen recurring ambiguity in prior private deployments: 

1) Control plane reachability: where the control plane endpoints live (customer VPC vs Redwood-managed BGP peer) and what explicit egress paths are allowed from control plane -> telemetry collectors.

2) Tenant routing / NAT behaviour: per-tenant SNAT vs shared NAT gateway approaches and how we express that in the routing matrix (attached). We prefer per-tenant SNAT for auditability but understand some DCs prefer consolidated NAT.

3) Egress separation and auditing: explicit egress channels for customer data (inference payloads) vs control telemetry (rollups/metrics/logs) and required audit logs for compliance (sample log attached).

Please review the diagram and call out any items that are unclear (labels, arrows, or dotted boundaries). Specific asks: 
- Lia: can you confirm whether EdgeWorks requires local NVA inspection for egress or if proxying to a centralized egress appliance is acceptable?
- Rajesh: if Palo Alto SD-WAN needs a particular BGP tag or community for routing tenant prefixes, include the exact tag value in the matrix.
- Aditya / Rishi / Soojin: please add inline comments on the control-plane hostname reachability and the proposed mTLS termination points.

Plan: we'll consolidate comments and push a v4 diagram before the 10:00 PDT review.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: anchored-vpc-diagram-v3.pdf (pdf), tenant-routing-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), egress-audit-sample.log (log)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Anchored VPC segmentation - diagram clarity & egress separation

Kimberly — quick pass with inline notes. High-level thoughts: 

- Control plane endpoints: prefer that control plane agents (heartbeat + orchestration) terminate into a customer-managed control subnet with an ingress ACL that only permits our collector IP ranges. That avoids opening a public-facing control endpoint.

- mTLS termination: recommend mTLS at the sidecar (node) and mutual auth at the controlplane load balancer; add a note on the diagram where the cert rotation boundary sits.

- Tenant NAT options: in the matrix I highlighted two rows where per-tenant SNAT is required for PCI workloads. For non-regulated tenants a shared NAT with distinct source ports + tag is ok, but logging must include tenant-id in the flow record.

Minor diagram edits: 
* Change label on the dashed line between CP and DP to "control-channel (mutual TLS)"
* Annotate the egress proxy with a sample CloudWatch/Stackdriver log path for auditability.

Link to annotated image: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAnchoredVPC (comments added).

I can grab the diagram and create a one-page callout of the control-plane lifecycle (certs, heartbeats, failover) if helpful.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lia Robinson <lia.robinson@edgeworks.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@paloaltopartner.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Anchored VPC segmentation - diagram clarity & egress separation

Hi team — thanks for the clear asks and the updated diagram. A few items from EdgeWorks' side: 

- Local inspection: our security team prioritizes local NVA inspection for tenant egress in production racks (we need to correlate tenant flows to tenant IDs at the NVA). That said, we can support a centralized egress appliance in staging for cost reasons; production should be local.

- BGP tagging: Rajesh confirmed offline that Palo Alto prefers community tag 64512:201 for tenant prefixes to trigger the local NAT policy. Rajesh: please reply-all with the exact community if that changes.

- Audit logs: the sample egress-audit-sample.log you sent looks fine. For SOC2 we need a retention policy of 90 days for raw flow logs and a 365-day index of aggregates. Can Redwood's telemetry pipeline support that retention or do we need to push to our S3?

Minor clarifications: the control-plane ingress ACL should list expected source IP ranges (we accept that changing ranges is normal; please provide an initial CIDR range list). Also, for mTLS, we need to ensure the cert subject includes the tenant id (or a consistent subjectAltName) to aid forensics.

We'll join the 10:00 PDT call and bring a security engineer (Rajesh will be there).

Thanks,
Lia Robinson
Head of Cloud Architecture
EdgeWorks Systems

--

Perfect — appreciate the quick turn. Next steps before the 10:00 PDT review: 

1) Aditya / Rishi: please add the control-plane CIDR ranges and cert-subject guidance to the diagram text layer (target: v4).
2) Rajesh: confirm the final BGP community value if it differs from 64512:201.
3) Lia: we'll surface two retention options in the playbook: Redwood-managed 90d raw + 365d aggregates (recommended) OR push raw logs to EdgeWorks S3 (if you prefer to own retention). Please flag a preference by EOD.

I'll produce v4 with the callout page and publish the Drive link pre-meeting. If we can get the CIDRs and community by noon PDT I can lock the diagram for today's runbook draft.

See you on the call.

Kimberly
